sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of this petition, the petitioner has prayed for quashing of FIR being C.R. No.
11192060240091 of 2024 registered with Viramgam Rural Police Station, District : Ahmedabad Rural as well as all other consequential proceedings pursuant to the aforesaid FIR.

entities.text: Viramgam Rural Police Station, District : Ahmedabad Rural
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The impugned FIR is registered on 3.3.2024 under Section 406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, by one Baldevbhai Shankarbhai Makwana against the present applicant and one NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined Gabhubhai Amthabhai Makwana, the present applicant is arraigned as accused No.2 in the FIR.

sentences.text: As per the contents of the FIR, it is stated that the complainant is the owner of an ancestral land being land bearing survey number of block No. 521 admeasuring 2327 sq.mtrs. and survey number of block No. 522 admeasuring 6769 sq.mtrs. and survey number 535 admeasuring 2327 sq.mtrs. at Village Charal, Taluka Sanand, District : Ahmedabad.

As the aforesaid land was acquired towards compensation, the complainant and other land owners received a total amount of Rs.1,12,28,300/-
and another Rs.12,00,000/- totaling around Rs.1,26,00,000/- which they wanted to invest in some other land and therefore, he was shown one of the land by his cousin Bhalabhai Karshanbhai being the land situated at survey No.530 at mouje Vadgas, Taluka Viramgam.

At that time, the accused No.1 Gabhabhai Amthabhai Makwana was present there NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined and he submitted that aforesaid land is very precious and he must buy that land at the earliest as there are other persons also ready to purchased that land and the land is going to fetch four times price than the price of the land at which is offered.

The deal was stark in Rs.96,00,000/- between the complainant and the accused No.1 posed someone as the owner of the land and he submitted to the complainant that if the owner of the land directly meets the complainant, he may ask for a higher price and therefore, he has given all the responsibility to sell the land and for a documentation to the accused No.1 and collected documents from the complainant.

3. Accused No.1 also submitted that the complainant will have to pay cash and therefore, on 20.10.2011, the accused No.1 and present applicant who happens to be wife of accused No.1 came to the resident of complainant and told that a sum of Rs. 11,00,000/- will have to be paid immediately and therefore, a sum of Rs.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined 11,00,000/-
were withdrawn from the bank and same was given to the accused No.1 and present applicant.
Thereafter, again on 18.11.2011, both the accused persons came to the resident of complainant and demanded a sum of Rs.50,00,000/-.
According to the FIR, the complainant and his brother in law Malubhai Khengarbhai took them to Sanand.

A sum of Rs.50,00,000/- were withdrawn and the amount was paid to the present applicant and thereafter, the accused No. 1 demanded Rs.25,00,000/- more by stating that the sale deed is ready and a draft was also shown to the complainant.
Thereafter, at the time when the complainant went to withdraw sum of Rs.25,00,000/- and the said amount was withdrawn and paid to the accused No.1.

Similarly, on 26.11.2011, a further Rs.10,00,000/- was withdrawn and paid to the accused No.1.
4.
Despite collecting all the aforesaid amount, the sale deed was not executed in favour of the complainant.
Thereafter, a long time has gone NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined by, despite that no sale deed was executed in favour of the complainant.

Every time, whenever the complainant used to asked the accused No.1 about execution of sale deed, he used to say that the land is an agricultural land and therefore, when the sale deed be executed, he is not in a position to say.
Thereafter, the accused No.1 also borrowed a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- from the complainant and a deed to that effect was also signed.

When the complainant asked for repayment of the aforesaid amount, accused No.1 used to give false and evasive replies and therefore, when the complainant threaten them to file a police complaint, on Rs.100/- Stamp paper, they gave in writing to the complainant that the sale deed in respect of a land Kanchanben Gabhubhai Makvana vs State Of Gujarat on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105973791/
2 belonging to Baldevbhai Shankarbhai Makwana would be executed within 20 days and the accused No.1 would execute the sale deed in respect of 10 wighas of land.

sentences.text: Thereafter, also from time to time false hopes were given just to ensure that no criminal case NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined is filed against the accused persons and ultimately, it had come to the knowledge of the complainant that the land in question is running in the name of one Bhulabhai Gandabhai and he has executed two different sale deeds on 10.10.2011.

He also found that some bogus documents were fabricated and he realized that he was cheated by the accused No.1 and present applicant to the tune of Rs.96,00,000/- and therefore, the FIR was lodged on 3.3.2024 for a transaction which has taken place in the year 2011 and onward.
5.
Learned advocate Mr. Mavadhiya submitted that the present applicant is not the beneficiary of the aforesaid amount alleged in the FIR.
She only happens to be the wife of the accused No.1 and she not being the beneficiary of the amount allegedly received by her husband, her case may be considered for quashing.

6. Except that no other submissions were made by learned advocate Mr. Mavadhiya.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined 7.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. Bhargav Pandya pointed out that the petitioner's anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. has already been withdrawn and the aforesaid fact has not been disclosed in the petition and therefore, the petition suffers from suppression of fact.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. Pandya also pointed out that a bare reading of the FIR constitute an offence and the present applicant has actively participated in the offence as the FIR categorically indicates that at least twice when a sum of Rs. 11,00,000/- were collected on 20.10.2011 and on 18.11.2011, when a sum of Rs. 50,00,000/- were collected from the complainant, the present applicant had accompanied the accused No.1 and both of them, jointly have received aforesaid amount totaling to Rs.61,00,000/- and therefore, as the bare reading of FIR constitution offence, this Court as per the settled preposition of law may not NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/6156/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/06/2024 undefined exercise the powers under Section 482 of Cr. P.C. and no indulgence be shown to the present applicant who has cheated the complainant by collecting a huge amount to the tune of Rs.96,00,000/-.
8. I have heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and perused the record.

On perusal of FIR, I found that the present applicant has actively participated in the offence in question and even the FIR also discloses an offence and therefore, in view of the aforesaid fact as the present applicant prima-facie has participated in the offence in question, considering her active participation, I don't see any reason to exercise the powers under Section 482 ready with Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Accordingly, the present petition lacks merit and same is required to be dismissed and the same is dismissed.

(NIRZAR S. DESAI,J) Pallavi Kanchanben Gabhubhai Makvana vs State Of Gujarat on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105973791/
